title: Entering the hospital on December 15 and the salt-free diet
summary: Carolyn Buck describes taking George Lewis to hospital with asthma and a sore throat, the doctors Hyman, the tent, the Hong Kong flu and his loss of appetite on a salt-free diet.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Okay, well, Karen, if you just heard from Simon.

Alright. Well, he entered the hospital about six o'clock in the morning. I think it was Sunday morning, December 15th. And at that time we both walked in together. It was a very cold, windy, rainy day. Evening, night, all night it had rained. And he hadn't wanted to go to the hospital, but he was complaining of a sore throat. And his asthma attacks were coming on pretty rapidly during the night. So I thought it best if I just called the doctor at the time I was bringing him in. And his doctor had been out of town, but fortunately the doctor's brother was in town, who is a heart specialist. He told me to bring him right in. What was his name? Dr. Hyman. Dr. Edward Hyman was his physician, but Albert Hyman was the brother who admitted him. And not knowing of his condition, somehow together we worked out what he should have emergency treatment. And he was immediately put into the hospital room. We got a room for him with nasal oxygen. And we found that the nasal oxygen was not doing what it should have been doing, so we put him in a tent. And at that time, knowing of his blood deficiency, he had a blood count, which had rapidly gone up over the past few months prior to his entering his past last visit at the hospital. It had gone up to normal, and I was kind of worried. And I asked the doctor, he had put him on medications which she was allergic to, which would thin his blood out again, and cause his blood count to go down. And he said at that time, we were trying to prevent pneumonia. He noticed that the x-rays came back, they were clear. His heart did to the cardiogram, it was favorable. And he thought possibly just a few days in the hospital would put him back on his feet. In the meantime, apparently this virus that was going around, I forget the name offhand, the Hong Kong flu, they classified it as a Hong Kong flu. And his doctor came in, and he was getting along fairly, fairly well. His appetite was going. He had been eating very, very well in the past nine months prior to his death. He couldn't get enough to eat. He could get up in the morning, and the first thing he would say would be, what are we going to eat today? And he would be prepared for three, four full meals. And his weight stayed. He would gain a few pounds. He hit 104, 105 a couple times. And then the edema set in from the heart condition. And we went up to 106 pounds, seven pounds. And after he entered the hospital, his appetite started failing, failing very, very quickly. In fact, it started, he worked on a Friday evening, and on Saturday afternoon, I gave him his supper. And he kind of picked on it, which is unusual for him. He said we'd eat it later, and he started getting drowsy. And they put him on a very, on a salt-free diet at the hospital. His own doctor was not in, and naturally being in a heart specialist, a heart specialist had put him on a salt-free diet. Anybody that's eaten salt-free food knows what it tastes like. So he just wouldn't eat. And eventually, before we knew it, he wouldn't eat at all. I mean, he just stopped eating. So I asked Dr. Edward Hartman whether we could put him on at least on a low-sodium diet, where he would be able to have some taste to his food. And he put him on it, it was about two days prior to his death, he put him on this low-sodium diet. But I do remember in the hospital, sneaking him a couple pieces of pie, when he wanted it at night. He would crave for something sweet, and I'd go down across the street, and go to the restaurant, and I'd get him a nice, big piece of apple pie, and he'd gulp it down. That's about all the solid food he'd had, hoping the doctor wouldn't find out about the sodium and the salt in it.
